reasons: The narrowed claim changes the quantified comparison family and therefore requires synchronized dependencies and free-symbol metadata.

narrow: The current statement confuses the greatest element of the full DMG equivalence class with the greatest element of its directed subclass.  On the one-vertex set, the graph containing only the directed loop is E-equivalent to the graph containing only the bidirected loop: for the sole nonempty endpoint pair, the cross-copy edge makes the unconditioned query dependent in both graphs, while conditioning on the sole vertex conditions the source endpoint in both graphs.  Hence the unrestricted union contains the bidirected loop and is not the directed greatest representative.  The proposed claim explicitly restricts the union to the published directed subclass; that subclass is strictly smaller than the full DMG class.

verdict.note: Accepted after Codex adjudication: one-vertex directed-loop/bidirected-loop E-equivalence falsifies the original unrestricted reduction; restricted directed-subfamily union matches the published directed theorem and leaves the unrestricted headline intact.
